fields.title: Polka: a deal blocked by architecture
fields.summary: The security team sent seven requirements; three come down to architecture.
fields.decisionPrompt: What do we answer and what do we do? Name the cost of your decision.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional grocery delivery service from local stores: 900 partner stores, a customer app, and a partner portal.
fields.brief/context: You are a Polka PM. The Domashniy chain has 40 stores and roughly 18% of potential turnover across three regions, and it is in the final negotiation stage. Signing was scheduled for three weeks from now. Yesterday, a list of requirements arrived from their security team. Three out of seven points come down to architecture.
fields.brief/objective: Fulfill the chain's requirements so the effort pays off for a segment, not just a single deal.
fields.brief/constraints: Three weeks until planned signing. 18% of potential turnover in three regions.
fields.brief/task: Decide what to answer the chain, what to do, and name the cost of the decision.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: An exception for a client and a product for a segment cost the same
fields.learnTakeaway/body: The difference between "we'll do it for them" and "we'll make a enterprise tier" is not technical—the work is the same. What differs is who pays for support a year from now and what you tell the next chain. The check is simple: have others asked for this? If they did and were refused, you are looking at an unformalized segment, not an exception.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: Data stored within Russia in infrastructure not shared with competitors. Updates in an agreed maintenance window, no more than once a month. Custom warehouse codes and price rounding rules in item cards.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: Shared schema, 900 partners in the same tables, partner-level filtering at the access layer. Updates continuous, for everyone at once. An extensions table for settings exists and is used by 6 chains.
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: "A separate installation takes six weeks, roughly 90k/month in infrastructure. Warehouse codes and rounding use the extensions table, take a week and a half, and work within the current schema. The update window in the shared schema is unworkable: we update everyone at once."
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: Two other chains asked about isolation over the past year. Both were refused. One left for a competitor.
fields.decisionOptions/0/label: Dedicated installation as an exception for this deal
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Six weeks. Covers all three requirements.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: the deal goes through with a three-week delay. The exception will have to be supported forever for free. The next chain will ask for the same, and there will be nothing to negotiate.
fields.decisionOptions/1/label: Enterprise tier with a dedicated installation
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Six weeks plus a week for packaging and pricing. Technically the same, commercially different.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: the deal is delayed by a month, with a risk of losing momentum. A product is created for the next chains—two known ones and an unknown number of those sales turned down. Infrastructure is paid for by the tier rather than eating into margin.
fields.decisionOptions/2/label: Fulfill two of three requirements, explain current setup for residency
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: A week and a half. Warehouse codes and rounding via extensions. On isolation: data is in Russia, separation is ensured at the access layer, we provide an audit.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: we meet the deadline. The security team's requirement is not met literally, and the decision depends on whether our explanation satisfies them. The update window cannot be met at all. Risk: the deal falls through at the last step.
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Drop requirements, sell as-is. Zero weeks.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: high probability of losing the deal and the third chain in a row. The product stays simple.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Failed to link the client requirement to the isolation model
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Missed the commercial dimension of the architectural decision
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Failed to isolate the irreversible decision about the tenant unit
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Client requirements were not translated into a spec section with verifiable points
